name: pwr
resume: All fifteen exports of pwr 1.3-0 match R. pnorm is erfc. qnorm and the t, F, and chi-square functions are SciPy. The root finder is R's zeroin. plot.power.htest draws the sample-size curve with Matplotlib. ggplot2 is suggested and is not translated.

proof.python:
import statistics
import time

from pwr import ES_h

def one():
    return ES_h(0.5, 0.4)

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(value)
print("%.17g" % statistics.median(elapsed))

functions.name: plot.power.htest
functions.done: The sample-size power curve. The check is those coordinates. Matplotlib draws the curve.

check.case: power curve of pwr.t.test(d=0.3, power=0.8); the time is the curve, not a graphics device

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(pwr))
one <- function() {
  x <- pwr.t.test(d=0.3, power=0.8, type="two.sample", alternative="two.sided")
  n <- x$n
  n_upper <- max(n * 1.5, n + 30)
  ss <- seq.int(from=10, to=n_upper, by=(n_upper - 10)/20)
  paste(sprintf("%.17g", sapply(ss, function(s) pwr.t.test(n=s, d=0.3, sig.level=x$sig.level, type="two.sample", alternative="two.sided")$power)), collapse=",")
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
if (is.character(value)) cat(value, "\n", sep="") else cat(sprintf("%.17g\n", value))
cat(sprintf("%.17g\n", median(elapsed) * 1000))
proof.python:
import statistics
import time

from pwr import plot_power_htest, pwr_t_test

def one():
    curve = plot_power_htest(pwr_t_test(d=0.3, power=0.8, type="two.sample"), draw=False)
    return ",".join(format(value, ".17g") for value in curve["power"])

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(value)
print("%.17g" % statistics.median(elapsed))
